learning_outcomes.text: Characterize the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties
Recognize and understand the principles of material science, technology, and chemistry applied to engineering
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully resolve new situations related to industrial engineering
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in various situations or before various audiences
Develop measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, task plans, and other works typical of the field of technical engineering
Apply the knowledge of industrial engineering to the learning of new methods and theories
Correctly and appropriately use specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards
Apply materials engineering to industrial problems
Recognize and understand the principles and fundamentals of materials engineering applied in the selection and characterization of materials

syllabus_topics: Block I: FUNDAMENTALS OF MATERIALS SCIENCE
Processes that take place by Diffusion
Tests: Tensile, Hardening, Fracture, Fatigue, Creep
Block II: MATERIALS AND THEIR TREATMENTS
Effect of some alloying elements in steel
Introduction and basic concepts about polymers
Properties and Applications of composite materials
Block III: OTHER PROPERTIES OF MATERIALS
Stages of Industrial Design: General Considerations
Material Selection Methods: Traditional, Graphical, and Databases
teaching_methods: Other methodologies (complementary activities, exercises, small evaluable assignments)
assessment_rules: Two partial exams will be conducted for theory (mixed tests) and problems (practical cases) covering the 1st and 2nd parts of the course. It is necessary to obtain at least 40% of the score in each of these mixed tests and practical cases to sum the rest of the grades obtained during the course. Assignments evaluate competencies such as analysis, writing, planning, and autonomy. Continuous assessment includes active attendance, participation in dynamics, debates, and continuous assessment tasks related to seminars and laboratory practices.
